assertions_contracts.best_practice: The hand-rolled sentinel pattern the guide prescribes now has a standard form: PEP 661's built-in sentinel type shipped in Python 3.15, designed exactly to distinguish 'argument omitted' from an explicit None with a readable repr.
assertions_contracts.evidence: The official 3.15 release announcement lists PEP 661 (sentinel built-in type) among the major new features.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: assert only for programmer invariants (python -O strips assert, so external rejection must be an explicit raise that survives -O); use a unique hand-rolled sentinel object to distinguish an omitted argument from explicit None; no mutation/authorization inside assert.

bounded_work.best_practice: No official Python source prescribes budgets; nothing contradicts it. 3.15's lazy imports and UTF-8-by-default change startup/encoding behaviour, not bounding obligations.
bounded_work.evidence: Tiger policy stricter than mainstream by design; no contradicting official position in the 3.14/3.15 What's New documents fetched.
bounded_work.guide_position: Named UPPER_SNAKE_CASE bounds for input bytes, item counts, nesting depth, retries, queues and captured output; no unbounded list(iterator) or task creation; retries need idempotency, a shared deadline, bounded backoff and injected jitter.

concurrency.best_practice: The landscape moved under the guide's framing: PEP 779 made free-threaded Python officially supported in 3.14 (not merely an experimental/optional configuration), 3.15 adds a stable ABI for free-threaded extensions, and PEP 734 (3.14) put multiple interpreters (concurrent.interpreters, InterpreterPoolExecutor) in the stdlib - an isolation mechanism the guide never mentions alongside its TaskGroup/process guidance.
concurrency.evidence: What's New in 3.14 documents PEP 779 (free-threaded officially supported) and PEP 734 (multiple interpreters in the stdlib); the 3.15 announcement lists the free-threaded stable ABI (PEP 803/820/793).
concurrency.guide_position: asyncio.TaskGroup for related tasks with admission bounded before creation; re-check state after every await; cleanup in finally and re-raise CancelledError; processes for killable untrusted work; guide says never assume the GIL and describes 3.14 free-threading only as 'optional free-threaded configurations'.

error_handling.best_practice: Matches current documented practice; 3.14/3.15 error-message improvements do not change exception semantics or chaining guidance.
error_handling.evidence: No exception-model change in What's New 3.14 or the 3.15 announcement.
error_handling.guide_position: Domain exception classes (or one explicit result type) per boundary; catch only what the layer can interpret; chain with raise DomainError(...) from exc; never swallow BaseException - interrupts and cancellation propagate; state whether failure leaves state unchanged or partial.

formatting.best_practice: Ruff's own project has deprecated the standalone Python language server (ruff-lsp) in favour of the native server built into the Ruff binary (ruff server), and the guide itself mandates Ruff's formatter as the single formatter - so the skill's black/ruff_ls references point at a superseded server and a formatter the guide forbids running in sequence.
formatting.evidence: The astral-sh/ruff-lsp repository carries a deprecation warning directing users to the native ruff server and to Astral's editor setup/migration guides.
formatting.guide_position: Guide: one configured formatter, Ruff's, with [tool.ruff] target-version py312 and line-length 100; validation runs ruff check and ruff format --check plus mypy --strict. SKILL.md metadata nevertheless says formatter: black and its compatibility line names diver's lsp/ruff_ls and formatters/black.

memory_ownership.best_practice: PEP 814 (Python 3.15) adds a built-in frozendict: a genuinely immutable, hashable mapping, which is a stronger primitive than the guide's frozen-dataclass-with-caveats approach for config/records that must not mutate.
memory_ownership.evidence: The official 3.15 announcement lists PEP 814 (frozendict built-in type) among the major new features.
memory_ownership.guide_position: Context managers (ExitStack/AsyncExitStack) own resources; never rely on __del__; bound caches/logs/queues; frozen dataclass preferred for records, with the explicit caveat that it is not recursively immutable when a field holds a list.

security.best_practice: The prohibitions hold, but 3.14 added a mechanism the guide's security section lacks: PEP 750 template strings (t-strings) return a Template separating static text from interpolations specifically so processors can sanitize/parameterize (SQL, HTML, logging) instead of concatenating untrusted values into a finished string.
security.evidence: What's New in 3.14 describes t-strings returning string.templatelib.Template objects whose parts stay separate before combination, and notes the sanitising use for user input.
security.guide_position: Never pickle.loads untrusted bytes or eval/exec external text; parameterized SQL; argv arrays with shell=False; validated URL schemes; venv is not a sandbox; subprocess with explicit argv/cwd/env/deadline/output bounds and a cleanup owner.

static_analysis.best_practice: mypy --strict remains a valid gate, but the field moved: Astral's ty (Rust, type checker + language server, from the Ruff/uv team) reached beta with Astral recommending it to motivated production users, and Meta's Pyrefly reached stable 1.x - the guide's 'choose one authoritative checker (mypy, or Pyright/basedpyright)' menu predates both.
static_analysis.evidence: Astral's ty announcement describes a beta type checker and language server designed as an alternative to mypy/Pyright and states Astral now uses ty exclusively in its own projects.
static_analysis.guide_position: Gate on mypy --strict; if Pyright/basedpyright is also used, choose one authoritative policy and explain differences instead of suppressing globally; Ruff provides lint diagnostics only (no type checking) in the guide's pairing.

testing.best_practice: Consistent with current practice; 3.15's new profiling package/Tachyon is an observability addition, not a testing-model change.
testing.evidence: No testing-semantics change in the 3.15 announcement affecting the guide's gates.
testing.guide_position: unittest or a reviewed runner; boundary cases (missing/false/zero/empty/max/oversize/wrong type/negative/exhaustion); validation also run under python -O; async timeout/cancellation/sibling-failure/stale-generation tests; property tests with bounded generators and reproducible seeds.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: Current major release is Python 3.15.0, released 2026-10-09 (PEP 810 lazy imports, PEP 686 UTF-8 by default, PEP 661 sentinel, PEP 814 frozendict, PEP 799 profiling). 3.14 is the previous bugfix branch; under the five-year release cycle a 3.12 floor is in security-only territory, so presenting 3.12+/3.14 as the 'primary target' understates the current baseline by a full major release.
toolchain_pins.evidence: Official Python blog announcement of the stable 3.15.0 release dated October 2026, fetched in full; guide's own Section 41 source links still point at docs.python.org/3.14 pages.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Primary target CPython 3.12+ with 3.14 behaviour called out; Ruff target-version py312; source list (P1-P6) links docs.python.org/3.14 pages; mypy --strict and Ruff versions pinned in dev dependencies.

current_versions.debugpy: Still the standard DAP implementation for CPython (Microsoft debugpy, via the Python extension ecosystem); 3.14 added a zero-overhead external debugger interface (PEP 768) underneath it - guide's debugpy pairing holds
current_versions.mypy: Still maintained and the guide's gate (mypy --strict); now has fast Rust competitors (ty beta, Pyrefly 1.x) the guide does not mention
current_versions.python: 3.15.0 stable, released 2026-10-09; 3.14 in bugfix maintenance; free-threaded build officially supported since 3.14 (PEP 779), stable ABI for free-threaded extensions added in 3.15
current_versions.ruff: Astral's linter+formatter; its native language server (ruff server, built into the ruff binary) replaces the deprecated standalone ruff-lsp package
current_versions.ty: Astral's Rust type checker + language server, in beta as of Oct 2026, recommended by Astral to motivated production users; absent from the guide
current_versions.uv: Matt's default package manager per workspace notes; guide requires a venv + pinned lock process, compatible with uv

mechanical_fixes.evidence: ruff_ls was the server of the standalone ruff-lsp package, which Astral has deprecated in favour of the native language server (ruff server); and the guide's own formatting rule mandates Ruff's formatter as the one formatter, with its review checklist ending 'one formatter (Ruff)' - black contradicts the guide itself.
Same internal contradiction: SKILL.md's own output contract and checklist require one formatter (Ruff), and the full guide's Section 23/27 configure and invoke only ruff format.

mechanical_fixes.correct: **Primary target:** CPython 3.15 (3.14 supported); Python 3.15 behavior called out explicitly
mechanical_fixes.current: **Primary target:** CPython 3.12+; Python 3.14 behavior called out explicitly
mechanical_fixes.evidence: Python 3.15.0 was released as the newest major release on 2026-10-09; the header's named 'current behaviour' version is a full major behind, and a 3.12 floor sits in security-only territory under the release cycle.

proposals.evidence: The official 3.15 announcement lists PEP 661 (sentinel built-in) and PEP 814 (frozendict built-in) as headline features of the current release.
proposals.proposal: On a 3.15 baseline, replace the hand-rolled 'unique sentinel object' idiom with the built-in sentinel type (PEP 661) for omitted-vs-None parameters, and offer frozendict (PEP 814) as the immutable-mapping primitive alongside frozen dataclasses where a mapping must be genuinely immutable and hashable.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt when the floor rises to 3.15; keep the hand-rolled idiom documented for 3.12-3.14 targets.

proposals.evidence: What's New in 3.14 documents t-strings producing Template objects that keep static and interpolated parts separate at runtime, explicitly enabling sanitising processors for user input.
proposals.proposal: Add t-strings (PEP 750, Python 3.14+) to the security section: for SQL, HTML and structured logging construction, accept a Template and process its interpolations (parameterize/escape) rather than receiving a pre-concatenated f-string, which destroys the static/interpolated distinction the check depends on.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as the preferred pattern for new 3.14+ code at injection boundaries; f-string-built queries stay banned as they already effectively are.

proposals.evidence: Astral's announcement positions ty as an extremely fast alternative to mypy and Pyright, designed around its language server, and states Astral uses it exclusively in its own projects while recommending the beta to motivated users.
proposals.proposal: Pilot Astral ty as the editor language server (and a non-gating CI job) while keeping mypy --strict as the authoritative gate until ty leaves beta; record the decision in the guide's 'one authoritative checker' rule so the menu reads mypy / Pyright / ty rather than mypy / Pyright only.
proposals.recommendation: Pilot only - do not swap the gate to a beta tool under Tiger Style's own evidence rules.
